title: Uruguayan migration law for nationals of Mercosur member and associated states

laws.title: Ley N.º 18.250 (Ley de Migraciones), consolidated text: art. 10 family reunification, art. 33 permanent residents, arts. 45 to 48 refusal, denial and cancellation, art. 72 reciprocity
laws.amendment: Amended by Acts of the General Assembly, often by articles in the yearly accountability laws (Rendición de Cuentas) or the 5-year budget law: art. 33 by Ley 19.254 and then Ley 20.075, art. 27 by Ley 20.075, arts. 45 C, 46 and 52 by Ley 20.212, arts. 24 and 26 by Ley 20.446 of 2025-12-16, the newest when read on 2026-11-11; the 2025 accountability law, Ley 20.531, changes none. IMPO shows each article's current wording with notes naming the law that gave it and the earlier wordings. The Executive regulates it by decree.

laws.title: Ley N.º 20.075 (Rendición de Cuentas, financial year 2021), art. 169: current wording of art. 33 of Ley 18.250, in force 120 days after promulgation on 2022-10-20
laws.amendment: Enacted once; the whole law's page on IMPO times out, and the article's own page shows art. 169 only as an asterisk and its own start rule, because the new wording lives in art. 33 of Ley 18.250. A later change to art. 33 shows in the consolidated text of Ley 18.250.

laws.title: Ley N.º 19.254 (2014), art. 2, original text: the earlier wording of art. 33 of Ley 18.250, with permanent residence for Mercosur nationals through the Foreign Ministry
laws.amendment: Published on 2014-09-04. Its art. 2 wording of art. 33 was replaced by Ley 20.075, art. 169; the text stays on IMPO as the original document and matters only for applications and dates before that change.

laws.title: Decreto N.º 45/023: regulation of art. 33 of Ley 18.250, requirements for Mercosur nationals (art. 2), consular applications (art. 4), transition (arts. 5 and 7), reciprocity (art. 8)
laws.amendment: An Executive decree, promulgated on 2023-02-08 and published on 2023-02-14; it repealed Decreto 312/015. A new decree amends or replaces it, with no fixed schedule; IMPO's notes on art. 33 of Ley 18.250 list the decrees that regulate it.

laws.title: Decreto N.º 394/009: general regulation of Ley 18.250, including criminal records (art. 4), length of permanent residence (art. 10), proof of a partnership (art. 16) and travel documents (art. 17)
laws.amendment: An Executive decree amended article by article by later decrees (for example art. 8 by Decreto 238/022, and art. 57 repealed by Decreto 441/011); IMPO shows the consolidated wording with notes. Decreto 45/023 refers to its art. 17 for the identity document of relatives of Uruguayans (art. 1).

laws.title: Ley N.º 17.927 approving the 2002 Mercosur Residence Agreements (the 4 members, and the members with Bolivia and Chile): art. 2 definitions, art. 9.2 family reunification, art. 11
laws.amendment: Treaties signed in Brasília on 2002-12-06 and approved by Uruguay by a single-article law promulgated on 2005-12-19; IMPO prints both texts. Any party may denounce them by written notice to Paraguay, the depositary, with effect 180 days after that notice (art. 16).

laws.title: Ley N.º 20.019 approving the Uruguay and Paraguay agreement of 2019-07-10 on permanent residence to reach free movement of persons (entry into force not confirmed)
laws.amendment: Approved by a law promulgated on 2021-12-23. It enters into force 30 days after the last diplomatic notice that each party has met its internal requirements (art. 12); no official text read shows that date, so whether it is in force is unconfirmed. It may be amended by written consent of both parties (art. 14) and denounced with effect after 180 days, sparing pending procedures (art. 13).

laws.title: Ley N.º 18.246 (unión concubinaria): 5 years of uninterrupted living together (art. 1), definition (art. 2) and judicial recognition fixing the start date of the union (arts. 4 and 5)
laws.amendment: Amended by Acts of the General Assembly, ad hoc: art. 19 was repealed by Ley 20.130 (2023) and art. 20 reworded by Ley 20.212 (2023); arts. 1 to 5 keep their original text. IMPO shows the consolidated text with notes.

laws.title: Código Civil (approved by Ley N.º 16.603), art. 280: majority at 18 completed years
laws.amendment: Amended by Acts of the General Assembly, article by article (art. 280 was last worded by Ley 16.719 of 1995); IMPO shows the consolidated text with notes. The whole Code's page times out; each article has its own page.

laws.title: Ley N.º 17.761 creating the indexed unit (Unidad Indexada, UI), whose value follows the consumer price index
laws.amendment: Not amended in IMPO's text. The law sets no amount after 2003-08-01: the value changes every day by formula, and the national statistics institute (INE) publishes the daily value (art. 4).

laws.title: Decreto N.º 239/026: residence by arraigo for people who entered before 2026-01-01 and are asylum seekers who withdraw their claim or were refused refugee status, regulating Ley 18.250
laws.amendment: An Executive decree promulgated on 2026-10-08 and published on 2026-10-26, in force 90 days after publication (art. 11), so not yet in force when read (a plain count of 90 days gives 2027-01-24). It builds on Decreto 138/024, which created the arraigo programme, and repeals provisions that conflict with it (art. 10).

laws.title: Dirección Nacional de Migración, Residencia Legal: the kinds of residence and the states it lists for Mercosur permanent residence
laws.amendment: A procedure page the migration directorate edits at any time, with no legal force of its own; it showed a last update of 2026-07-29.

laws.title: Dirección Nacional de Migración, Residencia Legal Permanente Mercosur: requirements, minors, fees and reciprocity exemptions
laws.amendment: A procedure page the migration directorate edits at any time, with no legal force of its own; it showed a last update of 2026-10-20. Its fees are in indexed units.

pitfalls.text: Art. 33, literal B, gives permanent residence to nationals of the Mercosur States Parties and Associated States who prove that nationality, but names no state. Among the texts read, the list of 11 (Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname and Venezuela) appears only on the migration directorate's pages. Because the statute refers to the association rather than to named states, a state that joins or leaves it changes who qualifies without a change to the law, and only the directorate's pages name the states.

Ley 20.075, art. 169, makes the current art. 33 apply from 120 days after the law's promulgation on 2022-10-20, 2023-02-17 by a plain count, not from 2023-01-01 like most of that law (art. 5). The same right already existed under the wording of Ley 19.254 (published 2014-09-04): application to the Foreign Ministry or a consulate, criminal records reported by the Ministry of the Interior within 15 business days, a Foreign Ministry decision within 30 business days, and requirements no stricter than for temporary residence. From Ley 19.254's entry into force until 2023-02-16 its wording applied.

Under the current wording of art. 33 (from 2023-02-17) the Ministry of the Interior decides, and an application may be filed with it or a Uruguayan consulate, which passes it on through the Foreign Ministry. Applications begun at the Foreign Ministry before the transfer are finished there (Decreto 45/023, arts. 5 and 7; art. 7 excludes those begun at consulates). The Uruguay and Paraguay agreement still names the Foreign Ministry for Uruguay (art. 3), which no longer agrees with the law.

The Ministry of the Interior must decide within 90 business days (días hábiles), not calendar days. INTERPOL and the scientific police have 15 business days to report on criminal records, after which the requirement counts as met unless they report otherwise. A person who applied at a consulate enters as a resident in process and, once the Foreign Ministry has sent the application on and the person is in Uruguay, has 30 business days to come to the directorate and complete the documents. If documents are missing for 365 days, the administration may go on to a decision.

The Residence Agreements count a naturalized national only after holding that nationality for 5 years (art. 2). Art. 33, literal B, asks only that the nationality be proved, and the Agreements yield to more favourable domestic rules (art. 11). Neither Decreto 45/023 nor the directorate's page mentions the 5 years, so no text read applies the condition to an applicant under art. 33, literal B; it may still matter where a family member's right rests on the Agreements.

Under the Agreements a national first gets temporary residence of up to 2 years, which can become permanent if the person applies in the 90 days before it expires (arts. 4 and 5). Uruguay grants permanent residence at once under art. 33, literal B, and the Uruguay and Paraguay agreement also asks no prior temporary residence (art. 2.2). Mercosur temporary residence (art. 34, last paragraph) is a separate choice for those who ask for it, not a step.

A family member who holds a listed nationality can apply in their own right under art. 33, literal B. One who does not gets, under the Agreements, a residence of identical term to that of the person they depend on, if they bring the documents and have no impediment, and applies at a consulate if their nationality needs a visa, unless Uruguayan rules waive it (art. 9.2). The directorate's page has no section for such a family member (only general requirements and minors), and Decreto 45/023 says the procedure follows the reciprocity agreement with the applicant's own state (art. 8).

Ley 17.927 approves 2 agreements, one signed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay and one that adds Bolivia and Chile, yet both define the States Parties as the members and associated states of Mercosur (art. 2). Whether art. 9.2 reaches family members of a national of Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname or Venezuela is therefore not settled by the Uruguayan texts; a reading limited to the 6 signatories is a choice, not the law's words.

The Agreements do not define family members and set no age. Art. 10 of the migration law guarantees reunification with parents, spouses, partners (concubinos) and unmarried children who are minors or adults with a disability. An unmarried adult child without a disability, a stepchild, a sibling or a grandparent is outside art. 10, so treating one as a family member is a reading. The list for temporary residents in art. 34 (spouses, minor children and parents) does not apply to permanent residence.

For the migration law a partner's status must be proved by a registered judicial recognition of the union (Decreto 394/009, art. 16). Under Ley 18.246 the rights of a union arise after at least 5 years of uninterrupted living together (art. 1), and the court's declaration fixes the date the union began (art. 5). Counting 5 years from the date a couple says it began, without a recognition, is not what the decree asks.

Majority is at 18 completed years (Civil Code, art. 280), and the marriage of a child also ends parental authority. Age also changes the file: under Decreto 45/023 (art. 2) only applicants over 18 sign the sworn statement on criminal records; Decreto 394/009, art. 4, literal A, says the requirement of that article does not apply to someone who has not turned 18 when the procedure starts; and the directorate asks a minor for a birth certificate and the express authorization of the parents with parental authority. No Uruguayan rule for a 29 February birthday was found.

Nationality alone does not guarantee the residence. It is denied to someone charged (formalizada) or convicted for an intentional common crime carrying more than 2 years of prison where committed, or with repeated offending, until 5 years pass without a new offence after serving the sentence (art. 46, as worded by Ley 20.212). Under Decreto 45/023, art. 2, applicants over 18 declare under oath that art. 46 and art. 45, literals B, C and D, do not apply to them, and criminal records are due from each country lived in over 6 months in the last 5 years; the directorate exempts minors.

Permanent residence lasts indefinitely, but the Ministry of the Interior may cancel it when the holder is absent from Uruguay for more than 3 years (art. 47, literal C; Decreto 394/009, art. 10). Neither text says whether the absence must be continuous or how it is counted. Cancellation does not take effect against a mother, father, spouse or partner (concubino) of a Uruguayan national (art. 48).

The directorate prices the residence at 557.30 UI plus a 55.70 UI migration certificate for the identity card, and 225.60 UI for each re-entry permit needed when leaving Uruguay before the residence is granted (Decreto 394/009, art. 15, provides the permit). Ley 17.761 makes the UI vary daily with the consumer price index (art. 2) and has the statistics institute publish the daily value (art. 4); the page says the amounts are based on UI whose value is readjusted every 6 months. Only the page says that Brazilians and Paraguayans pay nothing for permanent residence, by reciprocity.

The procedure follows the reciprocity agreement between Uruguay and the applicant's state (Decreto 45/023, art. 8), so fees and documents may differ by nationality. The Uruguay and Paraguay agreement, if in force, exempts permanent residence from costs (art. 4), which agrees with the directorate's exemption for Paraguayans; no Uruguay and Brazil agreement was read, so the Brazilian exemption rests on the directorate's page alone. The Executive may also suspend the benefits of the migration law for nationals of a state that restricts Uruguayans who settle there (art. 72).

IMPO lists Decreto 239/026 and Decreto 138/024 among the regulations of Ley 18.250, but they concern residence by arraigo for people who came in asking for refugee status, not art. 33. Decreto 239/026 admits only someone with no other path to permanent or temporary residence under arts. 33 and 34 (art. 2), so a Mercosur national who can use art. 33, literal B, falls outside it. It applies only from 90 days after its publication on 2026-10-26 (art. 11).

On IMPO an amending article such as Ley 20.075, art. 169, shows only an asterisk and a note, because the new wording is printed in the amended article of Ley 18.250. An earlier wording is on the original-document page.
